title: System status page surfaces service-wide (all-tenant) collection counts to every signed-in tenant key and sends that key to an endpoint that ignores it; Approver decision needed on exposure
evidence: apps/web/src/pages/system-status/statusClient.ts calls apiFetch('/health', apiKey) -> Authorization: Bearer <tenant key>. apps/api/src/server.ts mounts createHealthRouter BEFORE requireAuth, so /health is public and ignores the header. Counts are unscoped countDocuments across all tenants (qa/contracts/health-route.md C2), so the page shows tenants other tenants' activity volume. The web app does not know key scopes (AuthContext holds only apiKey), so the page cannot be gated on an admin-like scope client-side.
fix_direction: Approver decides: (a) accept (data already public to anyone reaching the API; page labels counts service-wide), or (b) hide the nav item/page unless a scope is known, which needs an API change exposing key scopes (e.g. via /keys). Independently, send the request without the Authorization header (needs a client.ts option; another lane owns client.ts) and drop the dead 403 'lacks the scope' branch (/health can never return 403). Note the contract qa/contracts/health-route.md C1 still says the shape is exactly {db, collections} while the route now also returns watchSilent/watchUnreadable and returns 503 when watchUnreadable>0 (ties to ISS-368).
reproductions: sed -n '60,80p' apps/api/src/server.ts -- health mounted before requireAuth.
notes: Not blocking PASS: no new data is exposed beyond unauthenticated /health. Medium for the key transmission + all-tenant volume visibility in product UI.
